chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

I asked him about taking out the meat of the sacrificial animals from Minā, and he said: We used to say that nothing should be taken out, because of the people’s need for it. But as for today, the people have become numerous, so there is no harm in taking it out. Thus, it does not contradict the first two reports, because it does not state in it that it is permissible to take out the meat of the uḍḥiyyah from what a person himself sacrifices or from what he purchases. So when that is not present in its apparent meaning, we interpret it to mean that whoever purchases from the meat of the sacrificial animals, there is no harm in his taking it out. And that which indicates this is...

key_terms.إِخْرَاجِ: removing or taking out from a designated place
key_terms.اشْتَرَى: purchased, indicating acquired meat rather than one’s own sacrificial animal
key_terms.الْأَضَاحِيِّ: the sacrificial animals offered at the appointed time
key_terms.الْخَبَرَيْنِ: the two prior reports being compared with this narration
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is unobjectionable
key_terms.لُحُومِ: the meat of slaughtered sacrificial animals
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the ritual location associated with hajj rites

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to take the meat of sacrificial animals out of Minā?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling on taking sacrificial meat out of Minā. It indicates that the earlier restriction was tied to people’s need, and that with changing circumstances and increased numbers, taking it out is no longer objectionable in that context.
